heading: Binary bit count via DP
body:
Every number **i** = `i >> 1` (the number with rightmost bit removed) + rightmost bit (`i & 1`).

**Recurrence**: `dp[i] = dp[i >> 1] + (i & 1)`

Reuse the count from **i/2** (already computed) and add 1 if **i** is odd.

heading: Why right-shift splits the problem
body:
`i >> 1` divides **i** by 2, effectively removing the rightmost bit. We've already computed how many 1-bits that smaller number has.

`i & 1` checks if the last bit is set (1 if odd, 0 if even).

This means **no need to count bits from scratch** — just look up and add.

q: What does `i >> 1` represent in the recurrence relation?
options: The number with the rightmost bit removed (i divided by 2)
The number with the leftmost bit removed
The remainder when i is divided by 2
explain: `i >> 1` shifts i right by 1 bit, effectively dividing by 2 and removing the rightmost bit. We've already computed dp[i>>1], so we reuse it.
